title: FDA Approves Treatment that Targets SMA Muscle Loss | Medical Devices and Pharma
summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Isembyld (apitegromab-mstn), the first therapy for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) designed to directly target muscle loss.

Isembyld is a monoclonal antibody, a type of biological drug, that works by inhibiting the activation of myostatin, a protein that normally limits muscle growth. Unlike gene therapies that address the genetic causes of disease, Isembyld targets muscle function directly.

title: FDA Grants Priority Review to uniQure's Huntington's Gene Therapy AMT-130, Decision Due May 2027
summary:
On November 2, 2026, uniQure announced that the FDA has accepted its biologics license application (BLA) for ifezuntirgene inilparvovec (AMT-130), a one-time gene therapy for Huntington's disease, and granted it Priority Review. The FDA set a decision date of May 1, 2027. If approved, it would be the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease.

...

AMT-130 uses an AAV5 vector to deliver a microRNA that silences the huntingtin gene, including a potentially highly toxic exon 1 protein fragment.
